messages.subject: Re: PD report not working
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jan-Philipp,

I will let others to comment on the format, but you are likely correct, this is likely due to a subsetting of the channels.

We do not recommend to subset the channels at the input stage. Even if you are not interested in comparing the other conditions, the remaining channels are useful for QC, and also for estimating the overall variability. A better workflow would be to use all the channels, and then compare the subset of conditions of interest using custom contrasts. See section 'MSstatsv4.0 Provides a Flexible Framework for Comparing Conditions'  in this manuscript <https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00834>.

I hope this helps at least somewhat
OV

messages.subject: Re: PD report not working
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jan-Philipp,

I am not sure what happens with the global median normalization (I will let others comment on this) but it is definitely not a good thing to do for TPP. I would set it to false.

Regarding the multi-plex comparison: indeed, if you use one channel as a reference (i.e., you equalize protein summaries in this channel between the plexes), then you can no longer use the channel for the downstream statistical analysis. This is because the normalization removes the variability in this channel. So my advice is to use another channel as the reference if possible (i.e., you assume that in that channel, there are no biological reasons for changes in protein abundance). If this is not possible and you want to proceed with the comparison, you can try reducing the peptide ions to a subset that is present in every plex. But  this is not great, as you will both lose many proteins and lose statistical power. Overall, having the right controls in a multi-plex TPP experiment goes the longest way.

HTH
OV

Devon

To be more specific on what MSstats does (ref: section 2.2 in page 10 of the MSstats manual <https://msstats.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/MSstats_v3.18.1_manual_2020Feb26-v2.pdf>) - once raw data (e.g. data from Skyline) is converted to MSstats format, the combination of values in the columns peptide sequence, precursor charge, fragment ion, and product charge uniquely determines a feature.  For each protein, MSstats determines the protein's intensity by taking a summarization of the intensities of the protein's features.
